excerpts:
# Iowa becomes first state to open applications for Workforce Pell Grant for people looking to learn a trade

By Lacey Reeves

Published: Jun. 11, 2026 at 11:50 AM CDT

Share

[Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.kcrg.com)

CEDAR RAPIDS, Iowa (KCRG) - Iowans wanting to learn a trade could have their training paid for by the federal government.

Iowa is the first state to open applications for a new Workforce Pell Grant. The program was created by the Big Beautiful Bill Act.

Iowans need to meet financial-need requirements to qualify. The grant will pay for non-degree training programs that are between 8 and 15 weeks.

Kirkwood Community College says this will help train students for entry-level jobs in health care, manufacturing and IT.

Colette Atkins, Kirkwood Vice President of Academic Affairs, said the program will be especially helpful for Iowans who can’t put their lives on hold.
“We have students that are working already and they can’t step away for two years, but can they step away to do that 8 to 15 weeks to get that training? They sure can. And now there’s financial support to help them do that. So it’s a win-win for our students and a win-win for our employers here in the state of Iowa,” Atkins said.

Kirkwood says it plans to offer training for people who can use the Workforce Pell Grant, and its working to get those programs established.

For more information on how the grant works and how people can apply click [here](https://educate.iowa.gov/higher-ed/financial-aid/workforce-pell "https://educate.iowa.gov/higher-ed/financial-aid/workforce-pell") .

results.title: UI research projects awarded grant development funding - The Daily Iowan
excerpts:
The University of Iowa’s Office of Vice President for Research awarded the first-ever Large Grant Development Opportunity to 12 research projects.

[Nolan Craig](https://dailyiowan.com/staff_name/nolan-craig/) , News Reporter

April 16, 2026

David Schwebel, vice president of research, chairs the event Scaling Your Research Program: From One Grant To Many at the College of Pubic Health Building in Iowa City on Tuesday, April 7, 2026. (Sal Yang/The Daily Iowan)

[Sal Yang](https://dailyiowan.com/staff_name/sal-yang/)

David Schwebel, vice president of research, chairs the event Scaling Your Research Program: From One Grant To Many at the College of Pubic Health Building in Iowa City on Tuesday, April 7, 2026. (Sal Yang/The Daily Iowan)

* * *

The University of Iowa’s Office of the Vice President for Research awarded funding to 12 research teams from a variety of disciplines through its first-ever Large Grant Development Opportunity program.
According to the [office’s website,](https://research.uiowa.edu/ovpr-awards-first-ever-large-grant-development-opportunity-funds-12-research-teams) the program began in 2026 and will run through 2029, awarding up to $270,000 across all three phases. The awarded teams are made up of a variety of disciplines, ranging from the colleges of Public Health to Liberal Arts and Sciences.

The grant was divided into three phases. Seven teams were awarded for the first phase, which aims to help build interdisciplinary teams and begin on pilot projects that could lead to further grants. The second phase, which no teams received, is the transition into the third phase, which was awarded to five teams, is focused on financially supporting these teams as they submit to larger competitive grants, according to the website.

One of these phase 1 grantees is an interdisciplinary effort to create a research center focused on the science of creativity. While the application was submitted by Dr.
Susan Shen an, assistant professor in psychiatry at the Carver College of Medicine, the project is a collaborative effort spanning six departments: Liberal Arts and Sciences, Education, Medicine, Engineering, Nursing, and Journalism and Mass Communications.

The researchers aim is to discover how to enhance and measure creativity, particularly among individuals with bipolar disorder. Shen said the focus will be on the creative process, rather than the creative product, to better understand the neuroscience behind it.

Shen said the project is unique to the UI, as it involves programs specific to the university, such as the Iowa Writers Workshop and the Writing Center, that will help exemplify the creative process through activities like writing.

A number of tests will be applied to research their effect on creativity, such as doing the activity before and after mood changes in bipolar individuals, or the use of artificial intelligence or psychedelics in other individuals, Shen said.
